cards.claim: Any vector A in a plane can be written as lambda*a + mu*b, a sum of real multiples of two given vectors a and b in that plane.
cards.quote: A can be expressed as a sum of two vectors — one obtained by multiplying a by a real number and the other obtained by multiplying b by another real number.

cards.claim: A unit vector has magnitude one, no dimension or unit, and only specifies a direction.
cards.quote: A unit vector is a vector of unit magnitude and points in a particular direction. It has no dimension and unit. It is used to specify a direction only.

cards.claim: The rectangular components of A are found by trigonometry from its magnitude A and its angle theta with the x-axis: Ax = A cos theta, Ay = A sin theta.
cards.quote: Using simple trigonometry, we can express Ax and Ay in terms of the magnitude of A and the angle θ it makes with the x-axis :

cards.claim: A vector in a plane can be specified either by its magnitude and its angle with the x-axis, or by its two components.
cards.quote: Now, we have two ways to specify a vector A in a plane. It can be specified by : (i) its magnitude A and the direction θ it makes with the x-axis; or (ii) its components Ax and Ay

cards.claim: Resolution along two given vectors a and b requires them to be non-zero and in different directions (non-collinear).
cards.quote: Let a and b be any two non-zero vectors in a plane with different directions and let A be another vector in the same plane

cards.claim: A component can be positive, negative or zero depending on the angle theta; components are not always positive.
cards.quote: As is clear from Eq. (3.13), a component of a vector can be positive, negative or zero depending on the value of θ.

cards.claim: OpenStax Example 2.5 (first leg): a 200.0 m displacement at direction angle 315 degrees has components Lx = +141.4 m and Ly = -141.4 m.
cards.quote: The components are L 1 x = L 1 cos θ 1 = ( 200.0 m ) cos 315 ° = 141.4 m, L 1 y = L 1 sin θ 1 = ( 200.0 m ) sin 315 ° = −141.4 m .
